intro: を marks the thing a verb acts on. が marks the thing a state is about. English blurs the two: 'I like cats' and 'I eat fish' look the same. In Japanese 好き is an adjective ('cats are likeable to me'), so cats are its subject and take が. Whether a noun takes を or が depends on the word that ends the sentence. Is it an action someone does to the noun? Or is it a state, or something that happens by itself?

skills.rule: Liking, skill, wanting, understanding and being able (好き, 上手, ほしい, わかる, できる) take が; a verb that someone does to the noun takes を.
skills.explain:
Q1. Is the predicate an adjective of feeling or skill? These are 好き, 嫌い, 上手, 下手, 得意, 苦手 and ほしい. Then が, and を is wrong: 猫が好きです, 車がほしいです. The person who feels it takes は: 姉はピアノが上手です.

Q2. Is it わかる, できる, 要る, ある, 見える or 聞こえる? These are states, so が: 日本語がわかります, テニスができます, 富士山が見えます.

Q3. Is it a potential form (読める, 話せる, 食べられる)? が is the standard choice, and を is also common in speech. Keep both in mind for these.

Q4. Is it a たい form (飲みたい)? Both を and が are correct. を is now the more common choice.

Q5. Otherwise it is an ordinary action verb, so を: ピアノを弾きます. Note that 好き and ほしい have verb partners that take を: 好む ('prefer') and ほしがる ('show signs of wanting').
patterns: [person] は [thing] が [好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手]
[thing] が [ほしい / わかる / できる / 要る]

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しい靴[くつ]{が}ほしいです。
日本語[にほんご]{が}わかりますか。
姉[あね]はピアノ{が}上手[じょうず]です。
examples.en: My sister is good at the piano.

examples.jp: 姉[あね]は毎晩[まいばん]ピアノ{を}弾[ひ]きます。
examples.en: My sister plays the piano every evening.

contrast.note: を needs an action verb that does something to the noun. 好き, 上手 and ほしい are adjectives, and わかる and できる are states, so nothing is being acted on.
が with an action verb makes the noun the doer: 猫が食べます is 'the cat eats', not 'I eat the cat'. When a real action verb follows, the thing acted on takes を.

mistakes.note: 好き is an adjective; the thing liked is its subject, marked with が.

mistakes.bad: 日本語[にほんご]{を}わかります。
mistakes.good: 日本語[にほんご]{が}わかります。
mistakes.note: わかる means 'is clear to me', so the thing understood takes が.

mistakes.bad: 車[くるま]{を}ほしいです。
mistakes.good: 車[くるま]{が}ほしいです。
mistakes.note: ほしい is an adjective; the thing wanted takes が.

skills.tip: Does the sentence end in an adjective or a state (好き, ほしい, わかる, できる)? Then が. Does it end in an action verb? Then を.

skills.rule: With a transitive verb (someone does it to X) X takes を; with its intransitive partner (X does it or it happens on its own) X takes が.
skills.explain:
Japanese has many verb pairs: 開ける / 開く, 閉める / 閉まる, 始める / 始まる, 止める / 止まる, 消す / 消える, 出す / 出る, 入れる / 入る, 落とす / 落ちる, 壊す / 壊れる, 変える / 変わる. The particle follows from the verb you choose. ドアを開けた: someone opened the door. ドアが開いた: the door opened, and no doer is mentioned.

To tell them apart, look at the endings. In a pair, the -su verb is the transitive one: 出す, 消す, 落とす. An -aru verb is almost always the intransitive one: 始まる, 閉まる, 決まる. -eru goes either way: 開ける is transitive, but 消える is intransitive.

States follow the same split: 窓が開いている ('is open'), 窓が開けてある ('has been left open', usually が).

One trap: verbs of leaving or passing through take を for the place, even when they are intransitive: 家を出る, 橋を渡る. This を marks a route, not an object.

examples.jp: ドア{を}開[あ]けてください。
風[かぜ]でドア{が}開[あ]きました。
examples.en: The door blew open in the wind.

examples.jp: 九時[くじ]に会議[かいぎ]{を}始[はじ]めます。
examples.en: We'll start the meeting at nine.

examples.jp: 九時[くじ]に会議[かいぎ]{が}始[はじ]まります。
寝[ね]る前[まえ]に電気[でんき]{を}消[け]してください。
examples.en: Please turn off the light before you go to bed.

examples.jp: 急[きゅう]に電気[でんき]{が}消[き]えました。

contrast.note: を goes with the transitive member: a doer acts on X (落とす, 'drop something'). With the intransitive member there is no object, so を is wrong (財布を落ちた).
が goes with the intransitive member: X changes by itself (落ちる, 'fall'). With the transitive member, が would make X the doer.
Intransitive motion verbs can still take を for the place that is left or crossed: 部屋を出る, 道を渡る. That is not an object, so it does not break the rule.

mistakes.bad: もうすぐ授業[じゅぎょう]{を}始[はじ]まります。
mistakes.good: もうすぐ授業[じゅぎょう]{が}始[はじ]まります。
mistakes.note: 始まる is intransitive (the class starts), so the class is the subject: が.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]で財布[さいふ]{が}落[お]としました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]で財布[さいふ]{を}落[お]としました。
mistakes.note: 落とす is transitive ('I dropped it'), so the wallet is the object: を.

skills.tip: Can you add 'by someone' to the action? Then use を with the transitive verb. Does it just happen? Then use が with the intransitive verb. In a pair, -su is transitive and -aru is intransitive.
